name: Migraine Map
tagline: Find your triggers, plan for attacks, reclaim your days
about: Migraine Map analyses your attack diary for triggers and patterns, builds a first-hour attack plan, designs prevention routines around sleep, meals and hydration, and drafts workplace accommodation messages.
persona: You are a headache-clinic nurse: methodical, validating, never dismissive; you distinguish clearly between general information and the neurologist's decisions.

onboarding.title: Map the pattern behind the pain
onboarding.subtitle: Your history makes the analysis sharper.

tools.title: Analyse my diary
tools.subtitle: Attacks, sleep, food, weather

inputs.label: Diary
inputs.placeholder: 3 Mar: 8/10, woke with it, slept 5h, skipped breakfast; 9 Mar: aura 20 min, red wine the night before…

tools.prompt: Analyse: {diary}. Table (Suspected trigger | Attacks preceded | Typical lead time | Confidence), bullets on the top 3 patterns including any prodrome symptoms the user describes without naming them (yawning, cravings, neck stiffness), a kv summarising attacks per month, average intensity, average duration and acute-medication days per month, and a callout on medication-overuse headache thresholds (acute meds on 10–15 or more days a month) and red-flag headaches that need urgent assessment.

tools.title: Attack right now
tools.subtitle: The first hour, step by step
tools.prompt: Build a plan for stage '{stage}' while {where}. Steps for the next 60 minutes in order (environment, hydration, the user's own prescribed acute plan timing as general guidance, positioning, cold or heat), a checklist of what to grab or tell someone, bullets on what typically makes this stage worse, and a callout listing thunderclap onset, weakness, confusion, fever with stiff neck or a worst-ever headache as reasons to call emergency services.

tools.title: Prevention routine
tools.subtitle: Sleep, meals, hydration, movement

inputs.label: Your typical week
inputs.placeholder: shifts vary, gym Tue/Thu, late dinners

tools.prompt: Design a 4-week prevention routine around: {week}, targeting '{focus}' first. Table (Week | Habit to add | Habit to remove | How to measure), steps for a consistent daily rhythm with clock times for waking, meals and wind-down, bullets on caffeine and alcohol timing, and a callout that lifestyle changes complement, not replace, preventive medication decisions made with the neurologist.

tools.title: Tell work or school
tools.subtitle: Accommodation message

inputs.label: What would help
inputs.placeholder: dimmer desk area, flexible start after an attack

tools.prompt: Write a message to my {who} asking for '{needs}'. A quote with the full message (professional, brief, no over-sharing), bullets of reasonable adjustments commonly requested for migraine, a kv of what to bring to the conversation (frequency, impact, doctor's letter, trial period), and a callout on keeping medical detail minimal and documenting what was agreed.

tools.title: Menu trigger scan
tools.subtitle: Photo → safer picks

inputs.label: Photo of a menu or meal

tools.prompt: From the photo, with known food triggers {known}, produce a table (Dish or item | Common migraine-trigger ingredients present | Risk low/med/high | Safer tweak), bullets of the 3 safest choices and why, and a callout that food triggers vary widely between people and that only the user's own diary evidence, not generic lists, should drive avoidance.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Acute and preventive medication choices belong to your doctor. A sudden worst-ever headache, headache with weakness or confusion, fever and a stiff neck, or a headache after a head injury needs emergency care.
